issues.description: The problem statement and template expect an interface named 'Rideable' (with method messageOnRide()), but the reference solution uses an interface named 'Mountable' and the file Rideable.java in the solution is empty. Several classes in the solution (Pig, Seal) implement Mountable instead of Rideable. This name/type mismatch between 'Rideable' and 'Mountable' will confuse students about which interface to create/implement and is structurally inconsistent across artifacts.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the interface name consistent across all artifacts. Either (a) rename Mountable in the solution to Rideable and ensure Rideable.java contains the messageOnRide() method and Pig/Seal implement Rideable, or (b) update the problem statement and template to use Mountable everywhere. Ensure the solution's Rideable.java is not empty and matches the interface expected by the assignment and template.

issues.description: The conceptually identical interface for animals that can be ridden is named 'Rideable' in the problem statement and the template Main.java, but the solution implementation uses the name 'Mountable'. This discrepancy (and the presence of an empty Rideable.java in the solution) creates a naming mismatch across artifacts and can confuse students about which interface to implement or use.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the interface name across all artifacts. Rename the solution's Mountable interface to Rideable (and update all implementing classes to 'implements Rideable'), or conversely rename uses of Rideable in the template/problem to Mountable. Prefer aligning the solution to the problem/template by replacing Mountable.java with Rideable.java (defining String messageOnRide()) and remove/replace the empty Rideable.java.
